children: Chalet Hotels is evolving from an asset-led hotel company into a broader hospitality platform, using Athiva, strategic partnerships and selective acquisitions to expand its portfolio while retaining an owner’s focus on asset value

Chalet Hotels has traditionally built its hospitality business around owning, developing and asset-managing hotels in high-barrier urban markets. Its portfolio now spans mainstream and luxury properties across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Delhi NCR, Rishikesh and Khandala. But the next phase is increasingly about how the company can grow beyond a purely ownership-led model.

That makes the perspectives of Shwetank Singh, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer; Gaurav Singh, Chief Operating Officer; and Manoj Agarwal, Chief Growth & Product Officer, Chalet Hotels, particularly relevant to the owners, developers and investors attending the Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards 2026 at JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. Their combined remit covers the company’s growth strategy, operations and product development as Chalet expands its own brand alongside global hotel partnerships.
From ownership to a hybrid growth model

Chalet currently operates 11 hotels with 3,389 keys. By September 2026, the company was targeting around 5,500 keys by FY2030, with the expansion coming through a mix of third-party-operated, franchised and Athiva properties alongside its owned assets. The strategy allows Chalet to pursue growth without relying solely on acquiring or developing hotel real estate itself.

The approach is already visible in recent projects. In August, Chalet announced two Athiva hotels in business-park environments: a 150-key property in Hyderabad and a 231-key hotel in Pune. Both are structured as long-term leases from entities associated with Mindspace Business Parks REIT, with the Hyderabad project involving the repurposing of an existing building and the Pune development being delivered on a grey-shell basis before Chalet undertakes fit-outs.
Athiva becomes the in-house growth engine

Athiva is central to that transition. Launched in 2025 with more than 900 keys across six identified properties, the premium lifestyle brand debuted with the 147-room Athiva Resort & Spa, Khandala. Chalet subsequently expanded its Athiva pipeline with the Hyderabad and Pune projects, taking the brand’s planned pipeline to around 1,200-1,300 keys by September 2026.

The model also gives Chalet greater control over product development and positioning, while allowing it to deploy the brand across different demand environments. Its latest projects place Athiva within established business ecosystems, where corporate demand, MICE and extended stays can complement the lifestyle proposition. For Chalet, the next hotel bet is therefore not simply about adding rooms. It is about choosing the right ownership structure, location, brand and operating model for each opportunity, while building Athiva into a meaningful part of the portfolio.
